text: Code refactoring is the process of improving the structure of existing code without changing what it does. The main goal is to make the code easier to read, understand, and maintain. Developers often refactor to remove duplication, simplify complex logic, or give variables and functions clearer names. It is important to remember that refactoring should not change the behaviour of the program, so tests are essential before and after the changes. By refactoring regularly, teams can reduce technical debt, which is the extra work that builds up when code is written quickly or poorly. In the long run, clean code saves time and money.
